To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a codimension-two E8 singularity with the Kodaira type I_0^{*} (1,1,2,2,4) in a F-theory compactification can lead to the following results.
(i) we found that a special type codimension-two singulartity in the E7/(SU5xU1)3 model can be used to realize a three-generation family unification model in F-theory.

(1) the six-dimensional spectrum of the E7 family unification model is realized in the codimension-two singling of F-theory, and (2) the three sets of three singlet pairs needed to explain the lepton-flavor mixing hierarchies are also present in the codimension two singularities of the E7 model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the three generations of fermion families can be unified with the three generations of Higgs families in a single E8 gauge group.
the question whether it is possible to construct a realistic model of family unification and large lepton flavor mixings from E8 singularity.
the question whether the observed pattern of fermion masses and mixings is a consequence of a simple and predictive theory, such as string theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a single E8 Kodaira singularity, when embedded into F-theory family unification, can give rise to the six-dimensional spectrum of the three-generation model and three sets of non-chiral singlet pairs needed for explaining the large lepton-flavored mixings in a seesaw scenario.

the E8 Kodaira singularity, which has been the most important singularity for the past 30 years, has now been shown to provide the most natural explanation for the three sets of singlet pairs needed in a seesaw scenario for the large lepton-flavour mixings and the Yukawa hierar-chies, and the most natural explanation as well for the six-dimensional spectrum with the same quantum numbers of the three-generation family-unification model.

the E8 Kodaira singularity provides the simplest possible family unification model with the correct number of families and the correct number of singlet pairs, and with a non-Abelian gauge group that can accommodate a large number of Yukawa couplings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a special class of codimension-two E8 Kodaira singularities can be used to realize a six-dimensional E8/(SO(10) x U(3)) family unification model with a set of six nonchiral singlets that have the correct U(3) charges to explain the Yukawa hierarcies and lepton-flavor mixing in a seesaw scenario.
the E8 codimension-two singulairty is a natural place for family unification.

the E8 codimension-two singulairty can be the origin of the six-dimensional spectrum and the three sets of the nonchiral singlets, which are the two key elements in the E7/(SU5 x U1^3) coset model, and that the lopsided textures of the neutrino Yukawa couplings are realized in a very natural way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the three sets of singlets can be naturally accommodated in a single family-unified E8 model.
the E8 Kodaira singularity, which is known to be a promising candidate for the GUT symmetry breaking, can also lead to a realistic model of family unification and lepton-flavor mixing.
the three-generation family structure and large lepton flavor mixings are not only consistent, but also naturally realized in a single E8 Kodaira singularity.
